children: Jefferies maintains concerns about long-end bonds, given potentially more risks from inflation and fiscal expansion, global economist Mohit Kumar says in a note. "We have been in the optimistic camp for the [U.S.-Iran] war and still believe that a deal, even if it's a fudge, may be feasible before the [U.S.] mid-terms," he says. "But we would still have the impact from El Nino and food prices," he says. In 2027, over 60% of European GDP is going through an election cycle, which implies a likelihood of fiscally supportive measures, Kumar says. "Hence, while we think that we could get a pullback in yields in the near term, our medium term view remains one of avoiding the long end and favoring steepeners on the curve." (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
